title: Open Ocean Surface Start
hook: Start 100 ft above the swells and fall through the waves.
expect: Watch the light change as you sink: red vanishes in the first 15 m, blue fades to black by a few hundred metres. A good first dive.

title: RMS Titanic
hook: Two halves, ~600 m apart, 3.8 km down.
expect: Total darkness, a debris field, rusticles, and marine snow. Bring the torch and move slowly.

title: Dean's Blue Hole
hook: A 200 m shaft into the Bahamian limestone.
expect: Entrance 25-35 m wide, flaring to ~100 m at about 20 m depth. Light drains as you sink; walls fall away into blue-black.

title: Challenger Deep (Mariana Trench)
hook: The deepest point on Earth, ≈ 10.9 km.
expect: Total black, silt plains, trench walls. Life is tiny and strange (hadal amphipods, snailfish). Plan to hover and listen.

title: Great Barrier Reef
hook: The brightest place in the app.
expect: Shallow, sunlit, saturated colour, corals and reef fish; mapped from the Allen Coral Atlas. Proof that the ocean isn't always dark.

title: False Bay, Seal Island (South Africa)
expect: Cold green water, fast silhouettes, and the occasional surface breach in home waters.
